instructions:
Drive Blender 5.2 through the 'Claude Blender MCP' add-on, mainly to make Roblox R6 animations.
Recommended workflow: r6_inspect_rig -> r6_list_presets -> r6_create_animation (preset) or r6_apply_clip (custom clip)
-> r6_preview (mode grid AND onion, from two views) -> r6_analyze -> fix the reported issues (r6_read_clip,
r6_get_pose, r6_set_keys, or r6_apply_clip with overwrite=true) -> r6_export -> after asking the user, push the
exported .lua into Roblox Studio with the Roblox Studio MCP tool execute_luau.
Joint angles use 'friendly' R6 values (documented in r6_apply_clip). Blender must be running with the add-on server
started (3D View > N panel > Claude tab).

tools.name: blender_ping
tools.description:
Check that Blender and the Claude add-on are reachable.

Returns the Blender version, the open .blend file, the add-on version, the list of available commands and any
command-module load errors. Call this first when something fails.

tools.name: blender_scene_info
tools.description:
Summary of the open scene: file, fps, frame range and current frame, active and selected objects, objects
(name, type, parent, visible, location, dimensions; capped at 300 with a 'truncated' flag), collections, actions.

tools.name: blender_object_info
tools.description:
Details of one object: world matrix, location/rotation/scale, dimensions, materials, modifiers, constraints,
parent, bone summary for armatures, mesh statistics.

tools.name: blender_execute_python
tools.description:
Run arbitrary Python inside Blender (escape hatch for anything the other tools do not cover).

Globals available: bpy, mathutils, Vector, Matrix, Euler, Quaternion, C (= bpy.context), D (= bpy.data),
view3d_context() (temp_override for the biggest 3D view, GUI only) and result (= None).
Assign `result = <JSON-friendly value>` to return data; print() output is captured.
Returns {"stdout", "stderr", "result"}. An undo step is pushed after the run (GUI).
Caution: this is real code in the user's Blender session. Never delete user data, save over files or touch
preferences unless the user asked. Prefer the dedicated r6_* tools for animation work. Blender 5.x uses slotted
actions: Action.fcurves no longer exists (use bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot).

Modeling: build meshes with bpy / bmesh (low poly, clean topology, real-world scale in studs: 1 stud = 1 Blender unit unless the scene says otherwise), add materials, then check the result with blender_viewport_screenshot. Export for Roblox with bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(filepath=..., use_selection=True) into the folder given by the Rovex tool description.

code.description: Python source executed inside Blender (main thread).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for Blender's answer (client side).

tools.name: blender_viewport_screenshot
tools.description:
Screenshot of the largest 3D viewport in the running Blender UI (PNG image + JSON with path and size).

Shows what the user currently sees. Not available when Blender runs in background mode; to look at an
animation use r6_preview instead (renders frames from chosen views, works everywhere).

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels.

tools.name: blender_set_frame
tools.description: Set the scene's current frame (updates the viewport and the evaluated pose).

tools.name: blender_set_scene_settings
tools.description: Change scene fps and/or frame range. Omitted values are left unchanged.

fps.description: Frames per second (Roblox animations usually 60 or 30).

frame_start.description: First frame of the scene range.

frame_end.description: Last frame of the scene range.

tools.name: blender_save_file
tools.description:
Save the open .blend file (in place, or as a new file when `path` is given).

Never overwrites a different existing file unless overwrite=true. Ask the user before saving their file.

path.description: Absolute .blend path for 'save as'. Omit to save the current file in place.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing a DIFFERENT existing file at `path`.

copy.description: With `path`: write a copy and keep working on the current file.

tools.name: r6_inspect_rig
tools.description:
Detect the R6 rig and describe it: chosen armature and bone mapping (Torso, Head, arms, legs), root controller
bone, HumanoidRootPart bone, RigMeta / rig_name (used for RBX_ANIMSAVES), scale (Blender units per stud), axes,
joint alignment check, constrained bones, weapon object, rig meshes, active action, alternative armatures,
warnings. Run this first on a new file.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_list_presets
tools.description:
List the built-in R6 animation presets: name, category, description, tunable params (with defaults and
descriptions), weapon hint, loop flag, plus library load errors.

Categories: locomotion (idle, walk, run, sprint, jump, fall, land, climb, swim, crouch...), combat (sword, greatsword,
spear, dagger, axe), skills (punches, kicks, bow, magic casts, dodges, rolls), reactions (hits, stagger,
knockdown, deaths, stun, emotes). Use r6_create_animation to build one.

category.description: Only presets whose category contains this text (e.g. locomotion, combat, skills, reactions).

tools.name: r6_create_animation
tools.description:
Build a preset animation at the scene fps and key it on the rig as a new Blender action (made active).

Returns {action, frame_start, frame_end, keys, bones_keyed, clip summary, weapon_attached, warnings}. Then
ALWAYS check it with r6_preview (grid and onion) and r6_analyze before exporting. To customize beyond params:
r6_read_clip -> edit the JSON -> r6_apply_clip(overwrite=true), or touch single frames with r6_set_keys.

speed.description: Playback speed factor (2 = twice as fast, fewer frames).

start_frame.description: Scene frame where the clip's frame 0 is placed.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing action with the same name instead of creating 'Name.001'.

attach_weapon.description: If the preset expects a weapon and that hand is empty, attach a placeholder.

set_scene_range.description: Set the scene frame range to the animation.

bake_step.description: 0 = key only the preset's key frames; N > 0 = bake every N frames (LINEAR keys).

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_apply_clip
tools.description:
Key a custom animation clip (JSON) onto the R6 rig as a new Blender action.

This is how to author any animation that is not a preset, or to re-apply an edited clip from r6_read_clip
(use overwrite=true to replace the action). Unspecified joints are interpolated from their own keys, the root
controller is keyed at rest, loops get cyclic curves, events become pose markers, and a 'Handle' joint keys the
attached weapon object. Returns {action, frame_start, frame_end, keys, bones_keyed, clip summary, warnings}.
After applying: r6_preview (grid + onion) and r6_analyze, then iterate.

FRIENDLY JOINT VALUES (what clips and every r6 tool speak)
- Joints: Torso (RootJoint), Head (Neck), Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, Left Leg, and optional Handle (weapon grip
  in the right hand). Aliases accepted: torso/root, head/neck, rarm/right_arm, larm, rleg, lleg, handle/weapon.
- rot = [x, y, z] degrees = CFrame.Angles(x, y, z) in the PARENT part's axes (torso axes for head and limbs,
  HumanoidRootPart axes for Torso), rotating about the joint pivot (neck, shoulder, hip, root).
  pos = [x, y, z] studs, extra offset in the parent's axes. Character space: +X right, +Y up, +Z back
  (the character faces -Z). A bare [x, y, z] means rot only. Missing rot/pos = [0, 0, 0].
  All zeros = Roblox rest pose (standing straight, arms and legs hanging down).
- Arms / legs: +x swings FORWARD (Right Arm [90,0,0] points straight ahead, [-30,0,0] swings back).
  Raise sideways (outward): Right +z, Left -z (Right Arm [0,0,90] = T-pose arm, [0,0,160] = above the head).
  Twist outward: Right -y, Left +y.
- Torso / Head: -x leans / looks FORWARD (down), +x leans back / looks up; +y turns LEFT, -y turns right;
  +z tilts LEFT, -z tilts right.
- Torso pos moves the upper body AND the legs hanging from it: pos [0,-0.2,0] lowers the body 0.2 studs (bob,
  crouch) but also pushes the feet 0.2 into the ground (ground = y -3 studs) unless the legs are angled
  (split stance, one leg +x the other -x). Keep dips small (-0.05 .. -0.35) and verify with r6_analyze.
- Handle (weapon joint, Part0 = Right Arm, C0 = Roblox RightGrip): rot/pos in the arm's axes about the hand grip.
  The blade/tip lies along handle +Y, so with rot [0,0,0] and the arm hanging the blade points forward like a
  Roblox Tool. Only key Handle when the weapon must rotate in the hand.
- R6 has no elbows or knees: expression comes from torso lean/twist/bob, head, shoulders, hips and timing.
  Typical amplitudes: walk legs +/-25..35, arms +/-20..40 opposite to the legs; run legs +/-45..60;
  idle breathing torso pos y 0..-0.05 and head 2..4 deg; strikes wind up (anticipation) before the hit.


CLIP JSON FORMAT (frames are clip-relative: 0 = first frame of the clip)
{"name": "Wave", "fps": 60, "length": 50, "loop": false, "priority": "Action",
 "description": "friendly wave", "weapon": null,
 "keys": [
   {"frame": 0,  "joints": {"Right Arm": {"rot": [0,0,0]}, "Head": [0,0,0], "Torso": [0,0,0]}},
   {"frame": 10, "interp": "BACK", "easing": "EASE_OUT",
                 "joints": {"Right Arm": {"rot": [0,0,150]}, "Torso": {"rot": [0,0,-4], "pos": [0,-0.03,0]}}},
   {"frame": 20, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,125], "Head": [0,0,-8]}},
   {"frame": 30, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,150]}},
   {"frame": 50, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,0], "Head": [0,0,0], "Torso": [0,0,0]}}],
 "events": [{"frame": 10, "name": "WaveStart", "value": ""}]}
- length = last frame. loop=true: the pose at frame `length` must equal frame 0 (repeat the first pose there).
- priority: Idle, Movement, Action, Action2, Action3, Action4, Core.
- interp = curve of the segment that STARTS at this key: BEZIER (default, slow-in/slow-out), LINEAR, CONSTANT,
  SINE, QUAD, CUBIC, QUART, QUINT, EXPO, CIRC, BACK, BOUNCE, ELASTIC. easing: AUTO, EASE_IN, EASE_OUT, EASE_IN_OUT.
  BACK + EASE_OUT = snappy overshoot; EXPO or QUART + EASE_IN = strike acceleration.
- A key may set only some joints; the others are interpolated from that joint's own keys.
- events become Blender pose markers and Roblox KeyframeMarkers (AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal(name)),
  e.g. "Hit" on the impact frame.
- weapon: {"kind": "sword", "hand": "Right"} (hint for previews) or null.
- Author in seconds: frame = round(seconds * fps). At 60 fps: walk cycle 40-60 frames, run 28-40, slash 20-35.

clip.description: Clip JSON object (format in the tool description).

start_frame.description: Scene frame where clip frame 0 is placed.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing action with that name.

set_active.description: Make the new action the rig's active action.

set_scene_range.description: Set the scene frame range to the clip.

bake_step.description: 0 = key only the clip's key frames (Blender interpolates). N > 0 = bake every N frames with LINEAR keys (exact match of the clip's own interpolation).

attach_weapon.description: Attach a placeholder for the clip's 'weapon' hint if that hand is empty.

match_scene_fps.description: Retime a clip authored at another fps to the scene fps.

close_loop.description: For loop clips, make the last frame repeat frame 0's pose.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_set_keys
tools.description:
Insert or replace keys on an existing action at given SCENE frames (surgical edits: fix one pose, add an
accent, push a contact pose lower...).

Joints not given in a key keep their current evaluated value at that frame; all six bones are keyed at each
listed frame. Read the current values first with r6_get_pose (same friendly units), then tweak.

FRIENDLY JOINT VALUES (what clips and every r6 tool speak)
- Joints: Torso (RootJoint), Head (Neck), Right Arm, Left Arm, Right Leg, Left Leg, and optional Handle (weapon grip
  in the right hand). Aliases accepted: torso/root, head/neck, rarm/right_arm, larm, rleg, lleg, handle/weapon.
- rot = [x, y, z] degrees = CFrame.Angles(x, y, z) in the PARENT part's axes (torso axes for head and limbs,
  HumanoidRootPart axes for Torso), rotating about the joint pivot (neck, shoulder, hip, root).
  pos = [x, y, z] studs, extra offset in the parent's axes. Character space: +X right, +Y up, +Z back
  (the character faces -Z). A bare [x, y, z] means rot only. Missing rot/pos = [0, 0, 0].

- Arms / legs: +x swings FORWARD (Right Arm [90,0,0] points straight ahead, [-30,0,0] swings back).
  Raise sideways (outward): Right +z, Left -z (Right Arm [0,0,90] = T-pose arm, [0,0,160] = above the head).
  Twist outward: Right -y, Left +y.
- Torso / Head: -x leans / looks FORWARD (down), +x leans back / looks up; +y turns LEFT, -y turns right;
  +z tilts LEFT, -z tilts right.
- Torso pos moves the upper body AND the legs hanging from it: pos [0,-0.2,0] lowers the body 0.2 studs (bob,

  Typical amplitudes: walk legs +/-25..35, arms +/-20..40 opposite to the legs; run legs +/-45..60;
  idle breathing torso pos y 0..-0.05 and head 2..4 deg; strikes wind up (anticipation) before the hit.


KEYS FORMAT for this tool = the clip "keys" entries below, but with SCENE frames (not clip-relative):
[{"frame": 31, "joints": {"Right Arm": {"rot": [40, 0, 10]}, "Torso": {"rot": [-8, 15, 0], "pos": [0, -0.1, 0]}},
  "interp": "BEZIER", "easing": "AUTO"},
 {"frame": 36, "joints": {"Head": [-5, 10, 0]}, "interp": "BACK", "easing": "EASE_OUT"}]

CLIP JSON FORMAT (frames are clip-relative: 0 = first frame of the clip)
{"name": "Wave", "fps": 60, "length": 50, "loop": false, "priority": "Action",
 "description": "friendly wave", "weapon": null,
 "keys": [
   {"frame": 0,  "joints": {"Right Arm": {"rot": [0,0,0]}, "Head": [0,0,0], "Torso": [0,0,0]}},
   {"frame": 10, "interp": "BACK", "easing": "EASE_OUT",
                 "joints": {"Right Arm": {"rot": [0,0,150]}, "Torso": {"rot": [0,0,-4], "pos": [0,-0.03,0]}}},
   {"frame": 20, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,125], "Head": [0,0,-8]}},
   {"frame": 30, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,150]}},
   {"frame": 50, "joints": {"Right Arm": [0,0,0], "Head": [0,0,0], "Torso": [0,0,0]}}],
 "events": [{"frame": 10, "name": "WaveStart", "value": ""}]}
- length = last frame. loop=true: the pose at frame `length` must equal frame 0 (repeat the first pose there).
- priority: Idle, Movement, Action, Action2, Action3, Action4, Core.
- interp = curve of the segment that STARTS at this key: BEZIER (default, slow-in/slow-out), LINEAR, CONSTANT,
  SINE, QUAD, CUBIC, QUART, QUINT, EXPO, CIRC, BACK, BOUNCE, ELASTIC. easing: AUTO, EASE_IN, EASE_OUT, EASE_IN_OUT.
  BACK + EASE_OUT = snappy overshoot; EXPO or QUART + EASE_IN = strike acceleration.
- A key may set only some joints; the others are interpolated from that joint's own keys.
- events become Blender pose markers and Roblox KeyframeMarkers (AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal(name)),
  e.g. "Hit" on the impact frame.
- weapon: {"kind": "sword", "hand": "Right"} (hint for previews) or null.
- Author in seconds: frame = round(seconds * fps). At 60 fps: walk cycle 40-60 frames, run 28-40, slash 20-35.

keys.description: List of {frame (scene frame), joints, interp, easing}; format in the tool description.

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_get_pose
tools.description:
Read the rig's pose at a frame as friendly joint values {frame, joints: {part: {rot, pos}}} (3 decimals),
directly reusable in r6_set_keys or a clip. Works on any animation, including hand-made ones.

frame.description: Scene frame; omit for the current frame.

root_motion.description: 'ignore_root' (default) removes the root controller motion, 'in_place' only its horizontal translation, 'full' bakes it into the Torso.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_read_clip
tools.description:
Read an action back as a clip JSON (same format as r6_apply_clip: friendly joints, interp/easing, loop,
priority, events). Edit it and re-apply with r6_apply_clip(overwrite=true) to change an animation globally.

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

frames.description: 'keys' = frames that have keyframes, 'all' = every frame, or an int step (e.g. 2).

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_preview
tools.description:
Render a preview image of an animation (Workbench, works without UI) and return it with a JSON summary.

Use it to SEE what you made: check silhouettes, readable key poses, arcs, foot contacts and weapon direction.
Good practice: a grid from 'three_quarter' plus a grid or onion from 'left' (side view shows leans, swings and
arcs) or 'front' (shows spread and balance). Takes a few seconds to a minute.

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

frames.description: Exact scene frames to show (max 24). Omit to sample `count` frames evenly over the action.

count.description: Number of sampled frames when `frames` is omitted (1-24).

view.description: Camera direction relative to the character.

mode.description: 'grid' = one tile per frame with the frame number (poses, silhouettes, contacts); 'onion' = all frames overlaid, older ones fainter (arcs, spacing, smoothness).

ground.description: Show a ground plane at the feet (judge contacts).

output_path.description: PNG path to write (default: a temp file).

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_analyze
tools.description:
Measure animation quality: foot contacts and ground penetration (ground y = -3 studs), planted-foot sliding
and implied ground speed with a suggested Humanoid WalkSpeed, loop seam error, max angular speed per joint with
spike frames, arm-torso and leg-leg interpenetration frames, root drift, and a list of human-readable `issues`
with severities. Fix every high/medium issue before exporting.

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

root_motion.description: Root controller handling, as for export.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_export
tools.description:
Export an action to Roblox (lossless Motor6D transforms sampled from Blender, then keyframe-reduced).

Files written to output_dir (stem = sanitized animation name):
- <name>.rbxmx : a KeyframeSequence model. In Studio: right-click ServerStorage > Insert from File..., or drag
  the file into the viewport.
- <name>.lua : a self-contained Luau script that rebuilds the KeyframeSequence and puts it in
  ServerStorage.RBX_ANIMSAVES.<rig_name> (folders created, same name replaced) and returns a short summary.
  To push it into an open Studio: read the file's full text and pass it as `code` to the Roblox Studio MCP
  tool execute_luau (datamodel_type "Edit", studio_id from list_roblox_studios). ASK THE USER before running
  code in their Studio. It also works pasted into Studio's command bar.
- <name>.json : the raw keyframe data (debugging / custom pipelines).
Then in Studio: select a rig whose model name is <rig_name> (see r6_inspect_rig; otherwise move the
KeyframeSequence into RBX_ANIMSAVES/<your rig's name>), open Animation Editor > ... > Load, check it, then
Publish to Roblox and use the asset id in an Animation (rbxassetid://ID).
Returns {files: {fmt: path}, keyframes, duration, animated_joints, grip, warnings}.

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

output_dir.description: Folder for the exported files (default: Rovex's blender-exports folder).

priority.description: AnimationPriority (default: from the action, else Action).

root_motion.description: 'full' keeps root controller motion in the Torso, 'in_place' removes horizontal travel (use for walk/run cycles driven by Humanoid movement), 'ignore_root' removes all of it.

reduce.description: Remove keyframes that interpolation reproduces within tolerance (smaller asset).

frame_start.description: First frame to export (default: action range).

frame_end.description: Last frame to export (default: action range).

angle_tol_deg.description: Reduction tolerance in degrees (add-on default 0.35; lower = more keyframes).

joints.description: Partial (layered) export: animate ONLY these joints (Pose.Weight 1). Their unlisted ancestors are written as identity Weight 0 poses (hierarchy only; HumanoidRootPart is always Weight 0) and every other joint is omitted, so a lower-priority animation (e.g. the base walk) keeps driving them. E.g. ['Right Arm', 'Handle'] for an upper-body weapon hold layered at Action priority. Omit to export every joint.

grip.description: Handle pose convention: 'tool' = Roblox Tool RightGrip (C0 = RightGrip C0, C1 = identity); 'weapongrip' = a Motor6D 'WeaponGrip' (Part0 Right Arm, C0 = CFrame.new(0,-1,0), C1 = the Handle's Grip attachment), converted as Rb*T*Rb^-1 with Rb the RightGrip rotation.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_attach_weapon
tools.description:
Put a weapon in a hand with the Roblox grip (RightGrip C0): a low-poly placeholder of `kind`, or an
existing user object. Parented to the arm bone, tagged claude_weapon, collection Claude_Weapons. The blade
points forward when the arm hangs. The right-hand weapon is the 'Handle' joint of clips and exports.
Returns {object, kind, hand, armature, bone, placeholder, replaced, grip}.

hand.description: Hand holding it. Omit for the default: Right, except shield and bow (Left).

object_name.description: Use this existing object (the user's own weapon model) instead of a placeholder. It is snapped so its origin sits on the grip, blade along its local +Z.

keep_transform.description: With object_name: only parent it, keeping its current world placement.

replace.description: Remove/release whatever that hand already holds.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_detach_weapon
tools.description:
Detach weapons: placeholders are deleted, the user's own objects are unparented in place and untagged.
Returns {detached, deleted}.

name.description: Weapon object name (see r6_list_weapons). Omit to detach every weapon of the rig.

hand.description: Without `name`: only detach the weapons in this hand.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_list_weapons
tools.description:
List weapon objects (claude_weapon tag): name, kind, hand, placeholder, armature, bone, animated; plus the
placeholder kinds available. With `armature`, only the weapons that rig holds.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_list_actions
tools.description: List the actions that animate this rig: name, frame range, r6 props (loop, priority, fps), is_active.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_set_action
tools.description: Make an action the rig's active action (what plays in the viewport, previews and exports by default).

name.description: Action to make active on the rig (see r6_list_actions).

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_mirror_action
tools.description: Create a left/right mirrored copy of an action (e.g. slash with the left side, dodge_left -> dodge_right).

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).

tools.name: r6_retime_action
tools.description: Create a retimed copy of an action (keys rescaled in time, events included).

action.description: Action name. Omit to use the rig's active action.

speed.description: Speed factor: 2 = twice as fast (half the frames), 0.5 = slower.

new_name.description: Name of the retimed action (default derived).

armature.description: Armature object name. Omit to auto-detect the R6 control rig (see r6_inspect_rig).
